Labour union to protest at party conference over migration curbs
Unison members to demonstrate for care workers to be excluded from Mahmood's visa reforms

Britain's biggest trade union will target Andy Burnham's first Labour conference as party leader to protest against Shabana Mahmood's migration reforms.

Unison is planning a demonstration outside the conference in Liverpool on Monday that will demand the party exempt care workers from stricter visa rules.

Under current migration laws, foreign care workers secure indefinite leave to remain (ILR) after five years, meaning they can settle in Britain.

However, Ms Mahmood, the Home Secretary, has proposed delaying the right to claim ILR from five to 15 years for foreign care workers, including those already in the UK.

Unison is calling on Mr Burnham and Ms Mahmood to keep the current five-year qualifying period for all skilled workers.

Andrea Egan, the general secretary of Unison, will be among the speakers at the protest outside the conference secure zone.

Ms Egan, who was expelled from Labour in 2022 and received the backing of Jeremy Corbyn, the former leader, will accuse ministers of having "broken promises" made to migrant care staff when they were recruited to work in Britain.

Unison said that staff who came to the UK "to ease the ongoing staffing crisis" would gather to express their opposition to the proposed visa changes.

The Prime Minister said at the time that he would rather retain the status quo of a five-year wait for ILR.

In July, Angela Rayner, the Housing Secretary, went public with her call for Mr Burnham to exclude care workers from the visa crackdown.
